findings.title: Comment and prose wrappers hide reserved unpacked assignments
findings.detail: Four bounded comment/prose wrappers contain literal reserved evidence or reencoding subscript writes in tuple, list or nested targets. Independently unwrapping the comment/prose prefix produces AST Assign nodes with reserved literal Store targets; no input is executed. Both classifiers return None in all 96 pairs across eight UTF encoding views and plain/gzip/XZ recovery. Sixty temporary plain working-file reads return byte-identical metadata across UTF8/16/32 and five suffixes. Equivalent ordinary comment/prose RHS/read expressions remain plain. AST parse discards commented text or rejects prose-prefixed syntax, while the lexical target expression still requires the closing bracket to lead directly to assignment/colon. Thus actual reserved assignment metadata in the packet-required comment-like/prose wrappers becomes ordinary content. Shared bound read and recovery/history/suffix code use this classifier; no synthetic commits/bound-read fixtures or complete task PASS forgery are claimed. Incidental for/with Store contexts are excluded from this finding. S1-S3 and S6-S10 reject in the independently reviewed forms, including the exact malformed/incomplete/string root probes.
